argument:
The trend evidence verifies — I re-ran the data: death cross confirmed, price below 20/50/200 SMAs (383.95/404.34/483.14), MACD -17.87 below signal, ADX 25.8, RS vs RSPH -38.0% over 63d. But three problems with this entry, one of them material:

(1) The ratio has already moved AGAINST the proposed entry. The proposal enters at 10.29, but pair-ratio now prints 10.4405 — the ratio is up ~1.5% from the fresh lows the proposal itself cites. ISRG returned +2.5% 1D and +4.5% 1W vs RSPH +1.2%/+2.2% — the idea leg outperformed the hedge by ~2.3pts over the past week. The violent mean-reversion bounce the originator names as risk #1 appears to have already started, and we'd be shorting INTO it with a stop at 10.75 only ~3% above the current print. From a z of -2.59 at the 2nd percentile, the path of least resistance on any good news is a squeeze, and the asymmetry here (target 9.55 = ~8.5% ratio downside, stop 10.75 = ~3% ratio upside) is fine on paper but the entry is stale by 1.5%.

(2) The valuation pillar is unverified by the originator's own admission (valuations 429'd; I confirmed the news tool returns 0 ISRG headlines this session — I got the same). A thesis whose core claim is 'structural multiple de-rating vs monopoly-era comps' that cannot state the current forward P/E vs ABT/TMO/JNJ is arguing the de-rating without measuring the multiple. Competition timing (Hugo placements, Ottava share) is asserted, not evidenced — no tool here verified a single placement datapoint.

(3) Event risk inside the horizon is mispriced in the sizing logic. US CPI prints 2026-08-12 (macro-events, high importance) — a premium-multiple, long-duration medtech name is a rates proxy both ways: hot CPI accelerates the de-rating (helps), cool CPI ignites the squeeze into the 10.75 stop (kills). Entering 4 days before a binary macro print with a 3% stop is a coin-flip overlay on top of the thesis.

My own angle adds one marginal support: ISRG carries meaningful OUS/Japan exposure in placements and procedures, and yen weakness is a translational headwind to OUS revenue — directionally consistent with the short, though I could not pull a verified USDJPY print this session to quantify it.

Recommendation: don't kill the thesis — the structural competition story and verified downtrend are real — but re-time it. The proposal's own catalyst language says 'failure of the ratio to reclaim the 10.7–11.0 zone on any bounce confirms distribution.' That IS the entry: let the bounce run into 10.7–11.0, short the failed reclaim with a tighter invalidation, rather than shorting at 10.44 with the stop 3% away and CPI on Wednesday. At the stated entry this is a chase at the 2nd percentile.
